The '''2024–25 season''' was '''[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]''''s 133rd season in their history and their 63rd consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2024–25 Premier League|domestic league]], the club also participated in the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], and the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. This was Liverpool's first season under new head coach [[Arne Slot]], who was announced as [[Jürgen Klopp]]'s successor on 20 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arne Slot to become Liverpool FC's new head coach |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/arne-slot-become-liverpool-fcs-new-head-coach |date=20 May 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

On 18 January 2025, Liverpool played their 6,000th competitive game since the club's inception in 1892, defeating [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] 2–0 in the Premier League thanks to two late goals from substitute [[Darwin Núñez]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool's 6,000th game: 13 stats to know ahead of Brentford clash |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpools-6000th-game-13-stats-know-ahead-brentford-clash |date=17 January 2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

On 27 April 2025, Liverpool were crowned Premier League champions after a 5–1 win at home against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], winning their first league title since [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20]] (and second in the [[Premier League]] era), their first [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on association football|in front of fans]] since [[1989–90 Football League|1989–90]] and a [[List of English football champions|record-tying 20th English league title]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Official: Liverpool are the 2024-25 Premier League champions |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/official-liverpool-are-2024-25-premier-league-champions |date=27 April 2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool win record-equalling 20th league title with rout of Tottenham |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/apr/27/liverpool-win-premier-league-title-by-beating-tottenham |date=27 April 2025 |publisher=The Guardian}}</ref> Arne Slot became the seventh manager in history to win the Premier League in their first season (and the first since [[2016–17 Premier League|2016–17]]).<ref>{{cite news |title=Managers to Win the Premier League in Their First Season |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/managers-to-win-premier-league-first-season |date=27 April 2025 |publisher=Opta Analyst}}</ref> In addition to winning the league, Liverpool scored in every away game in a league campaign for the first time in club history.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool achieve piece of club history for away goals in 2024-25 |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-achieve-piece-club-history-away-goals-2024-25 |date=19 May 2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

On 25 May 2025, Liverpool were presented with the Premier League trophy after a 1–1 home draw with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on the final day of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool share points with Crystal Palace before getting party started |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/25/liverpool-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report |date=25 May 2025 |publisher=The Guardian}}</ref> However, their title celebrations were overshadowed during their victory parade the following day on 26 May, when [[2025 Liverpool parade incident|a car drove into the crowd]], injuring many spectators shortly after the parade had finished.<ref name="ParadeIncident">{{cite news |title='It missed us by inches': Witnesses describe car driving into crowd at Liverpool FC parade |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy0jvepd1p2o |date=26 May 2025 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> This season also tragically marked the final campaign for [[Diogo Jota]], who died along with his brother [[André Silva (footballer, born 2000)|André Silva]] in a car accident on 3 July 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool forward Diogo Jota dies in car crash |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cr4we9z2l42o |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Diogo Jota: 1996-2025 |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/diogo-jota-1996-2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=3 July 2025}}</ref>

==First-team squad==
This season was the first since [[2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season|2015–16]] without [[Joël Matip]], and the first since [[2019–20 Liverpool F.C. season|2019–20]] without [[Thiago Alcântara]], who both retired from professional football after their contracts expired.

==Pre-season and friendlies==
[[File:Williams-Brice Stadium, Manchester United v. Liverpool, 8-3-2024.jpg|Pre-season friendly match against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], at [[Williams–Brice Stadium]] on 3 August 2024|thumb]]

On 23 February 2024, Liverpool announced they would return to the [[United States]] during pre-season, for matches against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to face Arsenal and Manchester United on return to USA for pre-season tour |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-face-arsenal-and-manchester-united-return-usa-pre-season-tour |date=23 February 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref> On 21 June 2024, Liverpool announced they would finish their pre-season programme with a match against [[La Liga]] side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at [[Anfield]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to complete 2024-25 pre-season with Anfield game against Sevilla |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-complete-2024-25-pre-season-anfield-game-against-sevilla |date=21 June 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref> An extra [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind-closed-doors]] friendly against [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] was later confirmed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool to host Las Palmas in behind-closed-doors friendly |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-host-las-palmas-behind-closed-doors-friendly |date=2 August 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

===Premier League===
{{main|2024–25 Premier League}}

On 25 May 2025, [[Mohamed Salah]] netted his 29th goal of the league season with an equaliser against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], which marked his 47th goal involvement of the season, setting a new record in a 38-game Premier League season, and equalling the previous record set by [[Alan Shearer]] and [[Andy Cole]] who did it in 42-game seasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Salah equals Premier League record for goal involvements |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4298728 |date=25 May 2025 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2024–25 FA Cup}}

As a Premier League side, Liverpool entered the FA Cup in the third round, and were drawn at home to League Two side [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League and Championship clubs entered the Emirates FA Cup in third round draw |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/dec/02/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-details-2024-25 |date=2 December 2024 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> where [[Rio Ngumoha]] made his senior debut and became the youngest Liverpool player ever to feature in the competition at 16 years and 135 days.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rio Ngumoha becomes Liverpool's second-youngest debutant |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/rio-ngumoha-becomes-liverpools-second-youngest-debutant |date=11 January 2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn away to Championship side [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth round proper draw has been confirmed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/jan/12/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-round-proper-draw-20251201 |date=12 January 2025 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2024–25 EFL Cup}}

As one of the Premier League clubs participating in European competitions, Liverpool entered the EFL Cup in the third round, and were drawn at home against Premier League side [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup Round Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/august/28/carabao-cup-round-three-draw-confirmed |date=28 August 2024 |publisher=English Football League}}</ref> They were then drawn away to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in the fourth round,<ref>{{cite news |title=Draw made for Carabao Cup Round Four |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/september/25/draw-made-for-carabao-cup-round-four |date=25 September 2024 |publisher=English Football League}}</ref> and away to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup: Quarter-Final draw |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/october/30/carabao-cup--quarter-final-draw |date=30 October 2024 |publisher=English Football League}}</ref> In the semi-finals, Liverpool were drawn against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], first leg away then second leg at home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup: Semi-Final draw |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/december/19/draw-for-carabao-cup-semi-final |date=19 December 2024 |publisher=English Football League}}</ref>

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2024–25 UEFA Champions League}}

As the third-placed team in the [[2023–24 Premier League|Premier League]], Liverpool entered the UEFA Champions League in the league phase.

====League phase====
{{main|2024–25 UEFA Champions League league phase}}

The league phase draw was held on 29 August 2024. Liverpool were drawn at home to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], [[Lille OSC|Lille]], [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]], and away to [[RB Leipzig]], [[AC Milan|Milan]], [[PSV Eindhoven]] and [[Girona FC|Girona]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Champions League league phase draw: All 36 teams learn their opponents |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0290-1bbaa109447c-6dbed8c6fe14-1000 |date=29 August 2024 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Revealed: Liverpool's league-phase opponents in 2024-25 Champions League |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/revealed-liverpools-league-phase-opponents-2024-25-champions-league |date=29 August 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

On 10 December 2024, Liverpool recorded their 150th win in European Cup history following a 1–0 win over [[Girona FC|Girona]] in the league phase.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool reach milestone of 150 victories in the European Cup |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-reach-milestone-150-victories-european-cup |date=10 December 2024 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}

As the first-placed team in the league phase, Liverpool entered the knockout phase directly into the round of 16.

=====Round of 16=====
The round of 16 draw was held on 21 February 2025. Liverpool were drawn against French champions and eventual winners [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], first leg away then second leg at home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Champions League round of 16 draw: Real Madrid get Atleti, Bayern face Leverkusen, Paris paired with Liverpool |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0296-1d1c270687d8-bdbd89f8cadc-1000 |date=21 February 2025 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

===Player of the Season award===
[[Mohamed Salah]] won the Player of the Season award for the fifth time, his fourth in the last five seasons which equals [[Steven Gerrard]]'s record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mohamed Salah wins Liverpool's Men's Player of the Season award for fifth time |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/mohamed-salah-wins-liverpools-mens-player-season-award-fifth-time |date=2 June 2025 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref>

==Parade incident==
{{main|2025 Liverpool parade incident}}

During the club's Premier League victory parade on 26 May 2025, a man [[Traffic collision|drove into a large crowd]] on [[Water Street, Liverpool|Water Street]]; 79 people were injured, 50 of whom were hospitalised. [[Merseyside Police]] arrested a 53-year-old man on the scene.<ref name="ParadeIncident" />
